questions.title: Two Sum
questions.prompt:
Given an array of integers `nums` and an integer `target`, return the indices of the two numbers that add up to `target`. Each input has exactly one solution, and you may not use the same element twice.

Example:
  twoSum([2, 7, 11, 15], 9)  ->  [0, 1]   (because nums[0] + nums[1] === 9)
  twoSum([3, 2, 4], 6)       ->  [1, 2]

questions.title: Reverse String
questions.prompt:
Given a string `s`, return it reversed.

Example:
  reverseString("hello")  ->  "olleh"
  reverseString("ab cd")  ->  "dc ba"

questions.title: Valid Palindrome
questions.prompt:
Given a string `s`, return true if it is a palindrome considering only alphanumeric characters and ignoring case.

Example:
  isPalindrome("A man, a plan, a canal: Panama")  ->  true
  isPalindrome("race a car")                       ->  false

input: A man, a plan, a canal: Panama

questions.title: Fizz Buzz
questions.prompt:
Return an array of length `n` (1-indexed). For multiples of 3 use "Fizz", for multiples of 5 use "Buzz", for multiples of both use "FizzBuzz", otherwise the number as a string.

Example:
  fizzBuzz(5)  ->  ["1", "2", "Fizz", "4", "Buzz"]

questions.title: Valid Parentheses
questions.prompt:
Given a string `s` containing just the characters '()[]{}', determine if the input is valid: brackets must close in the correct order and each closing bracket matches its opening type.

Example:
  isValid("()[]{}")  ->  true
  isValid("([)]")    ->  false

questions.title: Contains Duplicate
questions.prompt:
Given an integer array `nums`, return true if any value appears at least twice, and false if every element is distinct.

Example:
  containsDuplicate([1, 2, 3, 1])  ->  true
  containsDuplicate([1, 2, 3, 4])  ->  false

questions.title: Maximum Subarray
questions.prompt:
Given an integer array `nums`, find the contiguous subarray with the largest sum and return that sum.

Example:
  maxSubArray([-2, 1, -3, 4, -1, 2, 1, -5, 4])  ->  6   (the subarray [4, -1, 2, 1])

questions.title: Binary Search
questions.prompt:
Given a sorted (ascending) array of unique integers `nums` and a `target`, return the index of `target`, or -1 if it isn't present. Aim for O(log n).

Example:
  search([-1, 0, 3, 5, 9, 12], 9)  ->  4
  search([-1, 0, 3, 5, 9, 12], 2)  ->  -1

questions.title: Valid Anagram
questions.prompt:
Given two strings `s` and `t`, return true if `t` is an anagram of `s` (same characters, same counts).

Example:
  isAnagram("anagram", "nagaram")  ->  true
  isAnagram("rat", "car")          ->  false

questions.title: Move Zeroes
questions.prompt:
Given an integer array `nums`, move all 0's to the end while keeping the relative order of the non-zero elements, then return the resulting array.

Example:
  moveZeroes([0, 1, 0, 3, 12])  ->  [1, 3, 12, 0, 0]

questions.title: Climbing Stairs
questions.prompt:
You are climbing a staircase with `n` steps. Each time you can climb 1 or 2 steps. Return the number of distinct ways to reach the top.

Example:
  climbStairs(2)  ->  2   (1+1, or 2)
  climbStairs(3)  ->  3

questions.title: Single Number
questions.prompt:
Given a non-empty array `nums` where every element appears twice except for one, find and return that single element. Try to do it with O(1) extra space.

Example:
  singleNumber([4, 1, 2, 1, 2])  ->  4
